[dryly] Every customer has a limit: the most they'll spend. You never see it. You see an estimate, a range, and the real number is somewhere inside it. Not necessarily the middle. Psychology classes at Spirit University narrow it down. Nothing you sell can push the bill past their limit. They'll just say no.

[dryly] Watch their mood and their patience. Every pitch uses up a little patience. When it runs out, everything you do annoys them, and if they get angry enough they walk out and a rival gets the body. What a customer says is true. Someone clutching a photo loved the deceased: use Sympathy. Someone watching the clock didn't: Guilt works. Listen costs two patience and teaches you something new.

[dryly] Soft Sell deals you a hand of three extras; pick one that fits under the top of the estimate. Packages upgrade the embalming, flowers, plot, headstone and service, one step at a time. Hard Sell moves them up a casket. Coffee calms someone down, once per customer. A Discount takes a little off the bill and cheers them up, twice at most. Press Done when the bill is where you want it.

[dryly] After some funerals you'll prepare the body yourself, and there'll be a choice. A ring left on a finger. A fat wallet. Take it, or leave it. That's karma. Be good and the town trusts you: calmer, richer customers. Be bad and the money's nice, the hours are flexible, and the Guild pretends it doesn't know you.

[dryly] Cash is for the business. Di-Mart sells caskets wholesale; ask for Elijah, and don't let him touch your hair. Selling from stock pays better than a rush order.
